newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Bayernwerk seek reason for failed Hungary plant bid.
newsitem.headline: Bayernwerk seek reason for failed Hungary plant bid.

text.p: The German utility company Bayernwerk AG said on Tuesday it was seeking clarification over its failed bid to purchase the Hungarian Pecs power station in a tender that was declared unsuccessful in February.

"We are meeting (state privatisation agency) APV officials today," Bayernwerk Director Rainer Frank Elsasser told Reuters. "We heard that all bids had been declared invalid but we were never told why."
APV declared unsuccessful three tenders for coal-fired plants at Bakony, Pecs and Vertes for which four bids had been received. APV did not name the bidders.
On offer were over 61 percent stakes in Bakony and Pecs, each worth over nine billion forints at face valiue and an almost 75 percent stake in Vertes, worth 17 billion.
APV was reported to have said the main obstacle to the privatisation was unsatisfactory proposals on the integration of a number of mines and their employees, which are included with the plants.
Elsasser said Bayernwerk had put in a bid for Pecs in January and told a conference on Tuesday on power generation investment in Hungary that the bid was still on the table.
If Bayernwerk was to acquire Pecs, company plans included the possible replacement of the present plant by a new 200 megawatt station which would be cleaner and cheaper to run.
Bayernwerk currently has a 47 percent stake in regional electricity distribution company DEDASZ which serves the area around Pecs. It acquired the stake at the end of 1995.
